name: fillet_that_changes_radius
why: A fillet that goes from 3 to 8 along an edge of 40. THE NUMBER IS WHAT TELLS THE VARIABLE FROM THE CONSTANT: the volume removed by a fillet of radius r on an edge of length L is L*r^2*(1 - pi/4); for a radius that goes from 3 to 8 the mean of r^2 is (9 + 24 + 64)/3 = 32.33, and the calculation gives 277.5 mm3. A CONSTANT fillet of 3 would remove 77.3 of it, one of 8 would remove 549.4. The three numbers are far apart, and neither of the two wrong ones can pass for the right one.
_why_two_numbers: the operation reports both the material REALLY removed and the calculation redone by hand, and the case demands both. The real fillet is not exactly a linear sweep of the radius -- measured 277.7 against 277.5 of the calculation, 0.07% -- and that is why the calculation by hand is called «what is expected» and not «the right one».

expect.tolerance_why: it is the number MEASURED on this part; the half cubic millimetre covers the rounding of the answer, not a margin of opinion
40 * 32.333 * 0.214602: it is a closed calculation, and the tenth of a mm3 is the rounding

expect.why: the calculation by hand is declared approximate where it is reported, not in a note that nobody reads

expect.tolerance_why: 64,000 minus the 277.7 removed: the volume of the part confirms it from the other side
